title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How to Calculate Your Net Salary from the National Minimum Wage or an Award Rate
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay and estimate your net salary after tax and super. Includes the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, annual gross pay is about $52,270, with net salary around $41,400 after tax and Medicare, plus super of $6,272 paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and are often higher. For example, the Health Services Award and SCHADS Award have their own minimum rates. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides to ensure you're paid correctly.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my net salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When calculating annual net salary, remember that casual loading increases gross pay, but tax and Medicare are still deducted. Super is paid on the ordinary time earnings, which includes the loading.

faqs.q: Does the calculator assume I work 38 hours every week?
faqs.a: Yes, the standard full-time week is 38 hours. If you work fewer hours, your annual pay and net salary will be lower. The formula is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For part-time or casual work, adjust the hours accordingly. The calculator on this site uses 38 hours unless you change it.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Understanding Your Net Salary

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, it's natural to want to know what that means as an annual figure and, more importantly, what your **net salary** will be after tax and super. This guide walks you through the conversion, using the National Minimum Wage as a baseline, and explains how award rates and casual loading affect the numbers.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours. So:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 (rounded to $52,270)

If you're paid fortnightly, your gross pay is weekly pay × 2. Weekly pay at the minimum wage is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. For instance, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services (SCHADS) Award have their own pay structures. Always check your [pay guides](/blog) to see the correct classification and rate for your job.

Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, evenings, or overtime, which can significantly boost your annual pay. The calculation here assumes a flat rate with no penalties, so your actual earnings may be higher.

### Casual Loading

If you're a casual employee, you get a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. This loading is part of your ordinary time earnings and is included in the super guarantee calculation. When using the [timesheet](/) tool, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% to your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Estimating Your Net Salary

Your **net salary** is what you take home after tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the minimum wage example ($52,270 gross):

- Tax: ($52,270 – $18,200) × 15% = $5,110.50 (since $52,270 is under $45,000? Actually $52,270 is over $45,000, so need to calculate correctly: first $18,200 nil, then $26,800 at 15% = $4,020, then $7,270 at 30% = $2,181, total tax $6,201. Let's recalc: $52,270 – $18,200 = $34,070. But the bracket is 15% up to $45,000, so $45,000 – $18,200 = $26,800 at 15% = $4,020. Then $52,270 – $45,000 = $7,270 at 30% = $2,181. Total tax = $6,201.)
- Medicare: $52,270 × 2% = $1,045.40
- Net salary: $52,270 – $6,201 – $1,045 = $45,024 (approx).

Note: The on-site reference uses 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds, but for single taxpayers the reduction phase-out starts at $24,276, so most full-time workers pay the full 2%.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It does not reduce your net salary. For the minimum wage example, super is $52,270 × 12% = $6,272.40, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not included in your take-home pay but is a valuable addition to your retirement savings. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Fortnightly Perspective

Many employees are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is weekly pay × 2. For the minimum wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly net salary would be roughly $1,732 (based on the annual net divided by 26). This can help with budgeting.

### What This Estimate Doesn't Include

This calculation assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It uses the 2026–27 tax rates but Medicare reduction thresholds from 2025–26 (as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Always use the [reference tables](/data) for precise figures and consult a tax professional for your situation.

### Key Takeaways

- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour ($33.05 casual) – a starting point, but your award may pay more.
- Annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52. Assume 38 hours for full-time.
- Net salary is gross minus tax and Medicare. Super is extra.
- Use the [timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures, and check [pay guides](/blog) for your award.

Understanding your **net salary** helps you compare job offers and plan your finances. Whether you're on the minimum wage or a higher award rate, the formula is the same – just plug in your numbers.
